title: Isandro and the Witness
premise: When estate lawyer Isandro Vasquez is called to read the will of town founder Edmund Hale, the document is dated three days after Hale's official death—and when the town exumes Hale to settle the estate, the coffin is empty. Isandro discovers the will names a beneficiary who officially never existed: Hale's daughter, presumed dead forty years ago. As Isandro follows the paper trail, he realizes the killer is someone with intimate access to the case files—someone inside the investigation itself—and the missing body is the key to a forty-year cover-up of a murder the town's founding families committed together. Isandro traps the killer by staging a false announcement that the coffin has been found, forcing them to destroy the evidence, and the story ends with the town's beloved legacy dismantled and Isandro choosing the fragile found family of Hale's living daughter over the career he built on never losing.
about_author: D. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade reading other people's last words and never quite recovering from them. They write mysteries about paper trails, small towns, and the lies communities tell to stay standing.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Isandro Vasquez reads the will of town founder Edmund Hale to a packed courthouse, only to find its notarization date falls three days after Hale's recorded death. The beneficiary is a name Isandro doesn't recognize: Marisol Hale. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: professional pride curdling into unease—the first crack in his perfect record.

chapters.title: Empty Ground
chapters.summary: The court orders Hale exhumed to verify identity. Isandro watches from the cemetery fence as workers lift a coffin that weighs nothing—and inside there is nothing at all. Sheriff's deputy Dana Okonkwo, lead on the case, treats Isandro as a suspect. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: dread; the case has officially stopped being paper and started being bones.

chapters.title: The Daughter Nobody Buried
chapters.summary: Isandro traces Marisol Hale to a woman living quietly two counties over—alive, elderly, and terrified. She claims her father faked her death in 1985 to protect her from something, and she hasn't spoken to him since. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; Marisol becomes the case's human center.

chapters.title: Case File Ghost
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into the records room and removes pages from the original 1985 death certificate file—but leaves everything else untouched, including valuables. Isandro realizes the intruder knew exactly which documents mattered. POV: Dana Okonkwo. Emotional beat: the investigator's certainty begins to rot; the killer is inside the walls.

chapters.title: Founders' Day
chapters.summary: The town celebrates Hale's legacy with a festival while Isandro interviews the founding families' surviving heirs. Each alibi is airtight—too airtight, worded like rehearsed testimony. He notices they all use the same unusual phrase. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve; the town itself is a conspiracy wearing a parade.

chapters.title: What the Coffin Was For
chapters.summary: Dana, off the record, shows Isandro soil analysis: the coffin was buried empty from day one, meaning Hale's body was never in the ground—and Hale may have staged his own death. Then Dana's copy of the case file goes missing from her locked car. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: fear and betrayal; she's been played from inside her own investigation.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Marisol finally tells the truth: in 1985, the founding families killed a labor organizer, and Hale covered it up, faking his daughter's death to keep her silent and safe. The will is Hale's posthumous confession—and a trap he built for the people who helped him. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: grief and release; the theme of survival's cost made flesh.

chapters.title: Inside the File
chapters.summary: Isandro cross-references who could have known every detail of both the 1985 and current files: the town archivist, Hale's protégé, who has been 'helping' the investigation throughout. The archivist realizes Isandro knows. That night, Marisol's house is burned. She survives; her dog doesn't. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: rage—the case is now personal, and the clock is real.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin Trap
chapters.summary: Isandro leaks a false report that Hale's body has been found in the old mill, forcing the archivist to go destroy it before the excavation. Dana and Isandro wait in the dark. The archivist confesses mid-act: he helped cover up 1985 and killed Hale when the will surfaced. POV: Dana. Emotional beat: cathartic tension breaking—the trap snaps shut.

chapters.title: Reading the Will Again
chapters.summary: Months later, Isandro reads Hale's will a second time, publicly and truthfully: the estate goes to Marisol, and the town's founding myth is dismantled in open court. Isandro turns down the partnership that would have required discretion about the case, and instead helps Marisol rebuild. POV: Isandro. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; he lost the record, and gained a family worth more.
